texts: Repair by surgical valvotomy of the fused right and noncoronary commissures is not acceptable here: B.

In an adolescent with a thickened, tricuspid stenotic valve, commissurotomy gives a poor and short-lived result; balloon or surgical valvotomy belongs to infants and young children with a pliable valve.
A mechanical prosthesis, a bioprosthesis or a Ross operation are all reasonable, weighing anticoagulation, durability and growth.
In the picture, the robot, the rose and the tissue box are accepted, while the scissors are sent away.
Memory hook: a big teenager's stone mouth needs a new valve, not a snip.
